entries.question: Where do the specifications on a switch come from, and what am I looking at?
entries.answer:
Open the scan result and tap the Switches tab (or go to /switch-info/<rack id>). Pick the switch, and the card opens on the Specifications tab — the section headed "Hardware".

What you see there is the manufacturer's datasheet for the make and model RackTrack read off the chassis in your photo. It is not read live from the switch — nothing is queried over the network for this tab, so it works even when you are not on the switch's network.

The rows are a mix of two things:
1. A fixed set of labelled fields when RackTrack has them: Family, SKU, Ports, Port config, Uplinks, Max port speed (Gbps), Switching capacity (Gbps), Forwarding rate (Mpps), Buffer (MB), Latency (ns), MAC table, PoE, PoE budget (W), Power typical (W), Power max (W), Layer, Features, Rack units, Network OS, Status, Typical use.
2. Everything else pulled straight off the vendor's datasheet page, keyed by whatever wording the vendor used — which is why one switch shows a handful of rows and another shows dozens.

If a field is blank for that model it is left out rather than shown empty. Tap "View full details ↗" at the top right of the Hardware section to open the vendor's own product page in a browser and check anything that matters before you order or install.

Are these specs read from the switch
What is the Hardware section
One switch shows lots of specs and another shows only a few
entries.rootCause: The Specifications tab renders /api/specs, which returns a fixed set of SPEC_KEY_LABELS fields from the spec agent's record plus the agent's free-form extra_specs from the vendor datasheet; empty values are skipped.

entries.question: The switch card says "We couldn't identify this device from the rack photo" and there are no specs. What do I do?
entries.answer:
Type the make and model in yourself — the card has a built-in editor and the specs load as soon as you save.

1. On the Switches tab, expand the device (it will be titled "Unidentified device" or just show its U position).
2. Under the heading "Identification" you will see a "Not detected" chip and the line "We couldn't identify this device from the rack photo."
3. Tap "Enter make / model" on the right of that heading.
4. Fill in "Make / Vendor" (placeholder: e.g. MikroTik) and "Model" (placeholder: e.g. CRS328-24P-4S+RM). Both are required — Save stays greyed out until you have filled in both.
5. Tap Save. RackTrack immediately re-runs the spec lookup and the firmware check with your values, and the chip changes to "Manual entry".

Type the model exactly as printed on the chassis, including hyphens and any + signs. If you get it wrong, tap "Edit" and correct it, or tap "Clear" to remove what you entered and go back to whatever the photo produced.

Why it happens: RackTrack reads the make and model off the label in your photo. A device shot at an angle, in shadow, with the label hidden behind cables, or with no printed model on the front will come back blank.

entries.question: It got the brand right but the model is missing — "We identified "Cisco" but couldn't read the model. Specs and firmware checks need both."
entries.answer:
Add the missing half by hand. Specs and the firmware check will not run on a brand alone.

1. Expand the device on the Switches tab.
2. Under "Identification" you will see a chip reading either "Model not detected" or "Vendor not detected".
3. Tap the link on the right — it reads "Add model" when the vendor is known, or "Add vendor" when only a model was read.
4. Both boxes appear. Fill in the one that is blank, leave the other as it is, and tap Save.

The Specifications tab shows "Add vendor and model to see specs." until both are present, so once you save, reopen the Specifications tab and the spec table loads.

This half-detected case is common: the brand name is usually a big silkscreen logo that survives a bad photo, while the model number is small printed text on a sticker. If you can, get closer to the label and re-shoot the rack, or just type the model in.

entries.question: I typed in the make and model on the Switches tab, but my colleague still sees "Unidentified device" — and it vanished when I used a different phone.
entries.answer:
That is expected. A make/model you type on the Switches tab is saved only in the browser or app you typed it in. It is not sent to the server, so it does not travel to your teammates, to another phone, or to a browser where you cleared site data.

What it does do: it sticks on that device for you across reloads, and it survives a re-scan that reads different text off the label — the saved value is keyed to the device's serial number, MAC or U position, deliberately not to the make/model you can change.

If the whole team needs the corrected identity:
- Correct the device on the scan result itself instead. Open the device from the Device list and answer "No" to "Detected as <type> — right?" for the device type; corrections made there are saved to the scan and are visible to your organisation.
- For the make and model specifically, everyone who needs the specs has to type it once on their own device, or you re-shoot the rack with the label readable so the photo picks it up for everyone.

To remove your typed value, expand the device, tap "Edit" under Identification, and tap "Clear".
symptoms: My make/model correction isn't visible to my team
Manual entry disappeared on another device
Typed model didn't save for everyone
Manual entry chip only shows for me
entries.rootCause: saveOverride writes to localStorage under racktrack:<field>:<rackId>::<stableId>; there is no server round-trip, so the override is per browser profile.

entries.question: The specs shown are for a slightly different model number than the one printed on my switch.
entries.answer:
When the make and model came from the photo, RackTrack is allowed to correct what it thinks is a misread model number — so a label read as "C9300-46P" can come back with the datasheet for "C9300-48P". It only does this when the corrected model is very close to what it read, but on an unusual or brand-new SKU it can land on the wrong sibling model.

Fix it by telling RackTrack the exact model:
1. Expand the device on the Switches tab.
2. Under "Identification", tap "Edit".
3. Retype the Model exactly as printed on the chassis (hyphens, letters and any + signs included) and tap Save.

Once you have typed the model yourself, RackTrack treats it as confirmed and stops trying to auto-correct it — the specs you get back are for exactly the string you entered. The chip changes to "Manual entry" so you can see at a glance that the identity is yours, not the camera's.

Always sanity-check port count and rack units against the physical device before you rely on a spec sheet.
symptoms: Specs are for the wrong model
Model number shown doesn't match the label
Datasheet is for a similar but different SKU
Port count in specs doesn't match the switch
entries.rootCause: For OCR-sourced identities the server runs resolveAgentWithOcrCorrection, which may retry the lookup with a suggested model whose similarity score is >= 0.5; manually-entered identities set fromOcr=false and skip the probe.

entries.question: [Internal] How does the OCR model auto-correction work, and does the UI tell the user it happened?
entries.answer:
Internal only — do not describe this mechanism to customers beyond "RackTrack may correct a misread model number".

POST /api/specs takes an optional fromOcr flag. The Switch Information card sets it true only when the record came from the OCR pipeline AND the user has not manually entered a model.

When fromOcr is true, resolveAgentWithOcrCorrection runs two stages:
1. A DB-only probe (`--no-live`) on "<vendor> <model>". If it hits, return.
2. Otherwise take the agent's `response.suggestions`, score each against the queried model with _modelSimilarity (0.6 * shared-prefix ratio + 0.4 * in-order common chars over the longer string), and retry live with the best suggestion if its score is >= 0.5.
3. If that fails, fall through to a live lookup of the original query.

When a substitution happened the response carries matchedFrom (what OCR read) and matchedTo (what was looked up). Nothing in the client reads either field — the substitution is silent to the user. That is the root cause of "the specs are for a different model" tickets: the user has no in-app signal that the model was swapped.

POST /api/firmware does the same probe and then looks up firmware for matchedTo, so a bad substitution also skews the firmware verdict.
symptoms: User reports specs for a sibling model
matchedFrom / matchedTo in the API response
Why did the lookup use a different model number
entries.rootCause: resolveAgentWithOcrCorrection substitutes a similar model above a 0.5 similarity threshold and the client never renders matchedFrom/matchedTo, so the swap is invisible.

entries.question: How does RackTrack work out the make and model from a photo — and what can I do to help it?
entries.answer:
It reads the printed label on the front of each device. For every device the scan detected, RackTrack crops that device out of your rack photo, enlarges the crop, and runs text recognition on it three times (plain, contrast-boosted and sharpened) so faint text on dark plastic still comes out. It then works through the recognised text in this order:

1. Model-number patterns first. If the text contains something shaped like a known SKU — for example WS-C…/C9300-48P (Cisco), TL-SG… (TP-Link), DGS-/DXS- (D-Link), EX/QFX/MX/SRX (Juniper), CRS/CCR/CSS/RB (MikroTik), USW-/UDM/EdgeSwitch (Ubiquiti), GS/JGS/XS (NETGEAR) and others — that both gives the model and fixes the brand.
2. If no model pattern matches, it looks for a manufacturer name from RackTrack's vendor list.
3. If that fails, it looks for brand words like Catalyst, Nexus, Meraki, JetStream, Omada, ProCurve, PowerEdge, ProSafe, UniFi, RouterOS, FortiGate, DiskStation, and tolerates common misreads (Csco, Unfi, Mikrorik).

What helps, in order of impact:
- Shoot the rack straight on, not from the side — the label has to be square to the lens.
- Get light on the front panel; the label is usually small dark text.
- Move cables off the label if you can.
- Fill the frame with the rack so each device gets more pixels.

If it still misses, just type the make and model in on the Switches tab under "Identification" — that gets you the specs immediately.
symptoms: How does it know the brand of my switch
Where does the make and model come from
Why did it not read my switch label
How do I take a photo it can read
entries.rootCause: pipeline/ocr_devices.py crops each detected device, upscales to ~120px tall, runs three EasyOCR passes and parses make/model with per-vendor regexes, then the vendor sheet, then fuzzy brand keywords.

entries.question: My router / firewall / patch panel doesn't appear on the Switches tab. Where are its specs?
entries.answer:
The Switches tab lists switches only. A device the scan classified as a router, firewall, server, PDU or patch panel is deliberately left out of that list, even though it was detected in the rack and appears everywhere else in the result.

What to do:
- If it really is a switch and RackTrack labelled it as something else, correct the device type first: open the device from the scan result and answer "No" to "Detected as <type> — right?", then pick Switch.
- If the device type is correct and you just want the datasheet, use the standalone Specifications screen instead: it looks up any make and model you type, whatever the device class.

Worth knowing: RackTrack only tries to read chassis text at all on devices it classed as Switch, Server, Router, Firewall, Aggregation Core, Unidentified or Closed Unit. Patch panels, PDUs, UPS and blank panels are skipped on purpose — they rarely carry a model number on the front and OCRing rows of port numbers just produces noise.

Patch panel has no specs

entries.question: The Switches tab just says "Scanning…" / "Run a rack scan to detect switches." and never fills in.
entries.answer:
Reading the chassis labels is a separate, slower step that runs in the background after your scan finishes — it can take a couple of minutes on the server. Until it finishes, the Switches tab has nothing to list.

Do this:
1. Wait a minute or two, then leave the Switches tab and come back, or pull the page down / reload it. The tab does not keep retrying forever on its own — it stops checking after a short while and only looks again on a fresh page load.
2. If it is still empty after several minutes, check the scan actually found devices: the rack Overview should show a unit map with devices in it. No detected devices means nothing to read labels from.
3. If devices were detected but no switch was, the rack may contain no device classified as a switch — see the note about routers and patch panels not being listed here.

Older scans done before label-reading existed will also stay empty; re-scan the rack to get identification for it.
symptoms: Switches tab stuck on Scanning…
Run a rack scan to detect switches
Switch Information never loads
Switches tab empty after a scan
entries.rootCause: GET /api/scan/:rackId/ocr-devices returns 404 until ocr_devices.json exists; the prefetcher gives up after 8 consecutive 404s until the page is reloaded, and the empty state renders when the switch list is empty.

entries.question: [Internal] A rack keeps showing the same wrong make/model after re-processing. How is device identification re-run?
entries.answer:
Internal only.

Per-device label OCR is written once per rack to outputs/<rackId>/ocr_devices.json. scheduleOcrDevices() is a fire-and-forget spawn after a scan and returns immediately if that file already exists (or if device_unit_map.json is missing). Nothing in the normal flow ever regenerates it — a canonical refresh, a Netdisco resync, or re-opening the rack will all keep serving the original identification.

To force a re-identification for a rack: POST /api/scan/:rackId/ocr-devices. That runs pipeline.ocr_devices synchronously with a 5-minute timeout (EasyOCR on CPU is the slow path) and overwrites the JSON. GET on the same path only reads the cached file.

After a successful background run the server also rewrites the canonical scan result and reschedules the Netdisco sync so downstream consumers pick up real make/model instead of synthesized values.

Customer-facing wording: tell the user to re-scan the rack (which creates a new rack id, and therefore a fresh OCR run). Do not give customers the endpoint.
symptoms: Same wrong model after reprocessing a rack
ocr_devices.json not regenerated
How to force re-identification
entries.rootCause: scheduleOcrDevices short-circuits when outputs/<rackId>/ocr_devices.json exists, so identification is computed exactly once per rack id.

entries.question: How do I look up the datasheet for a device that isn't in a scan?
entries.answer:
Use the Specifications screen at /specifications (on a desktop or tablet it is listed as "Specifications — Vendor & model lookup").

1. Type the maker into "Make / Vendor" (placeholder: e.g. Cisco, Juniper, Aruba). A suggestion list appears as you type — tap one to fill the box.
2. Type the model into "Model" (placeholder: e.g. C9300-48P, EX4400-24T).
3. Tap "Get specifications". The button reads "Searching…" while it works.

You get a summary card with the vendor and model, a line reading "We pulled N specs from the vendor's product page — here are the most useful ones at a glance", and up to five headline rows chosen from Ports, Throughput, Layer, Form factor, Power, PoE, Uplinks, MAC table and Stacking.

Underneath there are two buttons:
- "Open product page ↗" — opens the vendor's own page in a browser.
- "Show all specs (N)" — expands the full table; it then reads "Hide all specs".

This screen is a pure lookup: it does not touch your rack, your scans or your CMDB, and nothing you type here is saved to a scan.

Specifications screen
Get specifications button
Look up specs without scanning
Show all specs
entries.rootCause: SpecificationsPage is a standalone /specifications route that POSTs a typed vendor+model to /api/specs and renders a highlights card plus an expandable full spec table.

entries.question: The vendor box doesn't suggest my manufacturer, or it says "Vendor list unavailable". Can I still search?
entries.answer:
Yes — type the vendor name in anyway and tap "Get specifications". The suggestion list is only a convenience; the lookup itself does not require the name to be on it.

Things to know about that list:
- It comes from RackTrack's vendor sheet on the server, loaded once when the screen opens.
- It only shows suggestions once you start typing, and never more than six at a time — keep typing to narrow it down.
- If the server could not supply it you get "Vendor list unavailable: …" under the box. The search still works.

If the lookup then comes back with no match, the vendor name spelling is usually not the problem — try the model number on its own form (exact SKU, hyphens included), or check the maker's own site. Very short or generic model strings are the most common cause of a miss.
symptoms: My vendor isn't in the dropdown
Vendor list unavailable
No suggestions when typing a vendor
Only six vendor suggestions
entries.rootCause: The type-ahead is populated from GET /api/specs/vendors (the vendor Excel sheet) and sliced to 6; POST /api/specs passes the typed vendor string straight through without validating it against that list.

entries.question: The Specifications screen shows "Both vendor and model are required." or an error about the backend / port 3001.
entries.answer:
Three different messages, three different causes:

"Both vendor and model are required." — you left one of the two boxes empty. Fill in both Make / Vendor and Model, then tap "Get specifications" again. Nothing was sent to the server.

"Backend returned a non-JSON response (HTTP …). Is the server running?" — the request reached something, but it did not answer with a result. Usually a server-side problem, not yours.

"Request failed: … Is the backend running on port 3001?" — the request never completed at all: no signal, no network, a VPN that just dropped, or RackTrack's server unreachable from where you are standing.

For the last two: check you have a working data or Wi-Fi connection, then retry once. If it keeps failing while the rest of the app works, report it to your administrator with the exact message and the make/model you typed — it is a server-side fault, not something you can fix on the phone.
symptoms: Both vendor and model are required
Backend returned a non-JSON response
Is the backend running on port 3001
Request failed on the Specifications screen
entries.rootCause: SpecificationsPage validates both fields client-side, then distinguishes an unparsable response body from a thrown fetch error and shows a different banner for each.

entries.question: I get "No spec match for …" or "Couldn't load specs." — is the model wrong?
entries.answer:
It means RackTrack has no datasheet for that exact make-and-model string: it was not in RackTrack's spec database, and the live search of the manufacturer's site came back with nothing usable in the time it had.

Try this, in order:
1. Check the model string. Type the SKU exactly as printed on the chassis — hyphens, letters and any + signs included (for example CRS328-24P-4S+RM, not CRS328). A shortened or partial model is the single most common cause.
2. Drop marketing words. Enter just the SKU, not the family name: "93180YC-FX", not "Cisco Nexus 93180YC-FX".
3. Check the vendor spelling matches how the maker writes it (TP-Link, D-Link, HPE).
4. Try again in a moment — the live search sometimes just runs out of time.

If the message you see contains developer text about installing requirements, ignore that part — it is a note meant for RackTrack staff and does not mean anything is wrong with your phone. Report it if you keep seeing it.

On a switch card, the same failure shows in the Specifications tab as "Couldn't load specs." — use the Identification editor to correct the model, which triggers a fresh lookup.

entries.question: The spec lookup spins for ages and then says the lookup took too long.
entries.answer:
A spec lookup that RackTrack has not seen before has to go out and read the manufacturer's site, which is slow and depends on that site responding. If it overruns, you get "Lookup took too long. Try again in a moment." or "Agent lookup took too long."

What to do:
1. Tap "Get specifications" again (or reopen the switch card). The second attempt is normally near-instant — anything RackTrack managed to fetch is remembered, so a repeat of the same make and model comes back from memory.
2. If it times out twice on the same model, the model string is probably one nothing can be found for. See the "No spec match" advice: use the exact SKU from the chassis.
3. This is server-side work, so a strong signal on your phone does not make it faster — but a dropped connection mid-wait will make it fail. Stay on Wi-Fi or a solid mobile signal while it runs.

A first lookup for a completely unknown model taking several seconds is normal, not a fault.
symptoms: Lookup took too long. Try again in a moment.
Agent lookup took too long
Looking up specs… never finishes
Specs take forever to load
entries.rootCause: Spec/firmware lookups spawn a Python agent per request with a 60s wall-clock budget (90s for the pipeline module path); on timeout the child is killed and a friendly error is returned. Results are cached in the agent DB and client-side per rack.

entries.question: It says "We found the product page but couldn't extract a spec table" — where are the specs?
entries.answer:
RackTrack located the manufacturer's page for your model but could not turn it into a table — some vendors publish specs as a PDF, an image, or behind a tab that has to be clicked.

Use the link instead:
- On the Specifications screen, tap "Open product page ↗" in the summary card and read the specs on the vendor's own page.
- If the lookup failed outright but a candidate page was still found, you get "Found a candidate page but couldn't extract specs:" followed by the link — tap the link.
- On a switch card's Specifications tab, the same link is "View full details ↗" at the top right of the Hardware section.

There is nothing to retry here; a different model from the same vendor will usually extract fine. If you need the numbers recorded against the rack, note them from the vendor page.

entries.question: What is the "Login portal" / "Vendor site" chip next to the switch name?
entries.answer:
It is a shortcut to the manufacturer's own website for the brand RackTrack identified, shown in the switch's title row next to its U position and IP.

- "Login portal" means RackTrack has the maker's actual customer/support sign-in page on file — tap it to sign in to that vendor and look up your entitlement, downloads or case history.
- "Vendor site" means RackTrack only has a general support or landing page for that maker.
- No chip at all means the brand did not match anything in RackTrack's list — usually because the make came back blank or as an unusual spelling. Fill in the make under "Identification" and the chip appears.

The chip opens in your browser, not inside RackTrack. RackTrack does not have your vendor account — you sign in with your own company's credentials on the vendor's site. Tapping the chip does not expand or collapse the switch card.
symptoms: What is the Login portal link
Vendor site chip on the switch card

entries.rootCause: SwitchCard calls findVendorLogin(effectiveMake) against a generated vendor→portal map; source 'login' renders the "Login portal" chip, 'fallback' renders "Vendor site", null renders nothing.

entries.question: In the port view, some downstream devices show a maker name and others say "Unknown". Where does that name come from?
symptoms: Downstream device shows Unknown instead of a maker
Where does the vendor name next to a MAC come from
MAC vendor is wrong
Device maker missing in the cables view
entries.rootCause: The client extracts the first 3 octets of each MAC and asks /api/oui/lookup, which reads the IEEE OUI table; prefixes registered as 'Private' are omitted when the table is built, so those resolve to null and render as unknown.

evidence.snippet:
// Entries registered as "Private" are skipped: the owner paid the IEEE to hide
// the name, so there is nothing useful to show.

// Cache misses too, as null — an unregistered prefix must not be re-asked.
      for (const p of missing) vendorCache.set(p, d?.vendors?.[p] || null);
